Get the Spatial Classifications of Municipalities

Source: R/raumgliederung.R
raumgliederung.Rd

Returns, for each municipality valid at a date, its code in the official spatial classifications (Raumgliederungen) of the BFS: language regions (SPRGEB2020), municipality typology (GDETYP2020_9, GDETYP2020_25), agglomerations (AGGL2020), the urban-rural typology (STALAN2020) and others. Use it to aggregate municipal data to regions or to stratify an analysis by settlement type.

Usage

raumgliederung(
  date = NULL,
  typology = NULL,
  lang = c("de", "fr", "it", "en"),
  cache = TRUE,
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

date

reference date, a Date or a string "YYYY-MM-DD". The default NULL uses today.

typology

optional character vector of classification codes or code prefixes, matched case-insensitively, e.g. "GDETYP2020". The default NULL returns all classifications.

lang

language of the labels, one of "de", "fr", "it", "en".

cache

logical; if TRUE, results are read from and written to the local cache (see cacheList()).

refresh

logical; if TRUE, the source is queried again even if a cached copy exists.

Value

A data.frame in long format with the columns stand_d, gem_id, gem_x, typ_c (classification) and value_x (code or label as delivered). The key is stand_d + gem_id + typ_c.

Details

The data come from the AGVCH levels service. The classifications available depend on the date; they are selected by name, never by column position.

Note

Experimental. The levels service documents its output columns only partially (they "vary with language, date and mapping configuration"); the result therefore keeps every classification column as delivered.

See also

gemeinde(), combineRegions() to draw the regions.

Other swiss.register: gemeinde(), gemeindeMutationen(), kanton(), praemienregion()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rg <- raumgliederung(as.Date("2021-01-01"), typology = "GDETYP2020_9")
} # }
